text: The Euclidean algorithm reduces a gcd computation using the identity gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, ___) for b ≠ 0, terminating when the second argument reaches 0.
explanation: Replacing (a, b) with (b, a mod b) shrinks the second argument (since a mod b < b) until it hits 0, at which point gcd(a, 0) = a is the answer; this runs in O(log min(a, b)) steps.
